item: Call Colorado's emissions referee before buying: how is a JDM 1994-97 Miata BP in a 1982 RX-7 tested (as the engine's year? tailpipe or OBD?), and does an aftermarket ECU (EMU PRO) pass
note: Prepared 2026-10-17. What the record already knows: after an engine change Colorado tests the newer of the car and the engine (5 CCR 1001-13 Regulation 11, rule 407.0), and an inspector fails every control if the DR 2365 form is not shown (K2, D-621). AirCare Colorado gives the OBD plug-in test only to vehicles 8-11 model years old and a dynamometer or idle tailpipe test to older ones, so a 1994-97 engine should be a tailpipe test, where the EMU PRO's lack of OBD does not matter. Call AirCare Colorado, 303-456-7090, and ask: (1) a JDM 1994-97 Miata BP in a 1982 RX-7 - is it tested as a 1994-97, and by tailpipe? (2) does a JDM engine with no US emissions label need anything beyond DR 2365 at a referee station? (3) is an aftermarket ECU allowed if the converter, O2 sensors, EVAP and PCV are there? (4) must the converter be CARB- or EPA-approved, and is a direct-fit universal one acceptable? Sources: aircarecolorado.com/need-know/faq; sos.state.co.us rule 407.0.
result: Must pass for the year of the engine (D-635); method and EMU PRO acceptance not stated
